align.collinear: points are in a line – place them in a triangle
align.hint: Select a splat and click points on its surface – point n pairs with point n of the reference
doc.reset-message: Are you sure you want to reset the scene?
doc.unsaved-message: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to reset the scene?
measure.length-tip: Enter the real length of the measured line: the whole model is scaled so it matches. Brings the splat to real-world size.
menu.collapse-tip: Collapse or expand the menu bar.
menu.edit.duplicate-tip: Copies the selected splats into a new layer. The original stays unchanged.
menu.edit.separate-tip: Moves the selected splats out of the layer into a new layer of their own.
menu.file.export.ply-tip: Uncompressed standard format that almost every splat program can read. Largest file.
menu.file.export.sog-tip: Highly compressed PlayCanvas format, ideal for the web. Much smaller than PLY.
menu.file.export.splat-tip: Simple, compact format of older web viewers. Stores only the base color, no view-dependent color.
menu.file.export.spz-tip: Compressed format by Niantic (Scaniverse), small and supported by many programs.
menu.file.export.viewer-tip: Exports the scene with a built-in web viewer as an HTML page or ZIP package that opens in any browser.
menu.file.reexport-tip: Repeats the last export with the same settings and overwrites the last exported file.
menu.select.delete-tip: Deletes the selected splats. Can be undone.
menu.select.lock-tip: Locks the selected splats: they are hidden and can no longer be selected or edited.
menu.select.reset-tip: Brings back all deleted splats of the selected layer.
menu.select.unlock-tip: Removes all locks. Locked splats become visible and editable again.
orient.align-tip: Rotates the model so the plane through the 3 points lies flat on the grid, for example a floor. The side facing the camera ends up on top.
orient.hint: Place 3 points to define a plane
panel.appearance.centers-selection-blend: How strongly the center dots of selected gaussians are tinted with the selected color.
panel.appearance.centers-unselected-blen: How strongly the center dots of unselected gaussians are tinted with the unselected color.
panel.appearance.centers.tooltip: Draw a dot at every gaussian center. Hidden while the overlays are toggled off ({{shortcut}}).
panel.appearance.gaussians-selection-ble: How strongly selected gaussians are tinted with the selected color.
panel.appearance.gaussians-unselected-bl: How strongly unselected gaussians are tinted with the unselected color.
panel.appearance.gaussians.tooltip: Render the gaussians themselves. Always rendered while the overlays are toggled off ({{shortcut}}).
panel.appearance.rings-selection-blend.t: How strongly the rings of selected gaussians are tinted with the selected color.
How strongly the rings of unselected gaussians are tinted with the unselected color.
panel.appearance.rings.tooltip: Outline the footprint of every gaussian. Hidden while the overlays are toggled off ({{shortcut}}).
panel.appearance.section-display.tooltip: Overlays drawn over the whole scene while editing. Press {{shortcut}} to toggle them all on and off without changing these settings.
panel.appearance.section-selection.toolt: Overlays drawn only for the selected gaussians. These stay visible when the display overlays are toggled off.
panel.appearance.selection-centers.toolt: Draw a dot at the center of each selected gaussian.
panel.appearance.selection-color.tooltip: Tint the selected gaussians with the selected color.
panel.appearance.selection-outline.toolt: Draw an outline around the silhouette of the selection.
panel.appearance.selection-rings.tooltip: Outline the footprint of each selected gaussian.
panel.appearance.size.tooltip: Size of the center dots in pixels.
panel.colors.apply.tooltip: Bakes the colour change into the selected gaussians, or the whole layer when nothing is selected. Locked ones stay unchanged. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
panel.colors.black-point.tooltip: Everything darker than this value turns black. Higher = deeper shadows.
panel.colors.reset.tooltip: Removes all colour changes already applied to the selected gaussians (the whole layer when nothing is selected).
panel.colors.temperature.tooltip: Warmer (positive, more red) or cooler (negative, more blue). 0 = unchanged.
panel.colors.tint.tooltip: Tints the gaussians with this colour (multiplied). White = unchanged.
panel.colors.transparency.tooltip: Changes opacity: left is more see-through, right more solid. 0 = unchanged.
panel.colors.white-point.tooltip: Everything brighter than this value turns white. Lower = brighter highlights.
panel.overlays.bounding-box.tooltip: Draws a white box around the selected splat object to show its extent.
panel.overlays.camera-poses.tooltip: Shows the cameras of the camera move as small camera icons in the viewport, keyframes as diamonds.
panel.overlays.dimensions.tooltip: Labels the edges of the bounding box with width, height and depth. Needs the bounding box turned on.
panel.overlays.frame-timings.tooltip: Shows how many milliseconds each frame takes to render. Use it to check whether a scene is too heavy.
panel.overlays.grid-planes.tooltip: Which planes the grid is drawn on: XZ is the floor, XY and YZ are vertical walls. Any combination works.
panel.overlays.overdraw.tooltip: Colours the image as a heat map: the brighter, the more gaussians overlap at that spot. Shows where rendering gets expensive.
panel.settings.fly-speed.tooltip: How fast the camera moves in fly mode with the WASD keys and the mouse wheel. 1 = default.
panel.settings.fov-dolly.tooltip: On: changing the field of view moves the camera in or out so the subject keeps its size (dolly zoom). Off: the camera stays put and zooms like a lens.
panel.settings.sh-bands.tooltip: How much view-dependent colour (sheen, reflections) is shown. 0 = base colour only, 3 = full quality.
panel.settings.stochastic-alpha.tooltip: Fast render mode without sorting, slightly grainy. Movement: only while the camera moves or while editing; Auto: only when the scene gets too slow; Enabled: always.
panel.settings.tone-mapping.tooltip: How bright colours are mapped to the screen. Linear leaves them unchanged; ACES, Filmic and the others compress highlights like film.
panel.splat-data.camera-depth-tip: Distance in front of the camera along the view direction. Changes when the camera moves.
panel.splat-data.dc-tip: Raw value of the base colour without the view-dependent part (DC coefficient).
panel.splat-data.distance-tip: Distance of the splat from the world origin (0, 0, 0).
panel.splat-data.histogram-tip: Drag to select all splats in the marked value range. Shift adds, Ctrl removes, Shift+Ctrl keeps only the overlap.
panel.splat-data.hue-tip: Hue as an angle 0–360° (0 = red, 120 = green, 240 = blue), as it appears from the current view direction.
panel.splat-data.quaternion-tip: One component of the splat's rotation (quaternion). Rarely useful for selecting.
panel.splat-data.sh-tip: Raw value of a view-dependent colour component (spherical harmonics, SH).
panel.splat-data.surface-area-tip: Measure of the splat's extent (sum of the squared sizes). Helps to find large, flat splats.
panel.splat-data.volume-tip: Size X × Y × Z of the splat. Helps to find very large or tiny splats.
popup.about.title: About
popup.export.animation-tip: Takes the camera move from the timeline into the viewer. Only available when camera keyframes are set.
popup.export.compress-ply-tip: Saves as .compressed.ply: much smaller file, slightly lossy, nearly invisible splats are removed. Not every program can open it.
popup.export.fov-tip: Viewing angle of the viewer camera in degrees. Higher values show more but look wider. 50–70 is typical.
popup.export.invalid-filename: Enter a valid filename without reserved names or characters.
popup.export.iterations-tip: Passes of the SOG compression. More passes match the colors more closely but take longer. Default: 10.
popup.export.loop-mode-tip: What happens when the camera move ends: stop (None), start over (Repeat) or run back in reverse (Ping Pong).
popup.export.overwrite-message: This file already exists. Overwrite it or choose a different filename.
popup.export.sh-bands-tip: How much view-dependent color (sheen, reflections) is stored. 0 = base color only and smallest file, 3 = full quality.
popup.export.spz-version-tip: SPZ 4 is the current format. Only pick SPZ 3 if an older program cannot read SPZ 4.
popup.export.type-tip: HTML: a single file with viewer and scene that opens straight in the browser. ZIP package: viewer and scene data as separate files, e.g. for uploading to a web server.
popup.lod-select-message: This file contains multiple levels of detail. Select which one to load.
popup.lod-upload-note: Note: you can upload scenes with LODs directly at
popup.overwrite-source: This file is in use by the current scene and can't be overwritten. Choose a different filename.
popup.publish.allowance-used: You've used today's {{limit}} publishing allowance. You can publish again in {{time}}.
popup.publish.destination-tip: New scene creates a new publication. Picking a scene from the list updates that scene instead.
popup.publish.generate-lods-required: Required for scenes with more than 40 million splats.
popup.publish.generate-lods-tip: Builds levels of detail: the viewer loads a coarse version first and streams finer parts as you get closer. Recommended for large scenes with many splats.
popup.publish.message: Use the link below to access your scene.
popup.publish.override-animation-tip: Replaces the camera move of the chosen scene with the current one from the timeline.
popup.publish.override-model-tip: Uploads the current splats and replaces the model of the chosen scene with them.
popup.publish.please-log-in: Publishing to PlayCanvas requires a user account. Please log in and try again.
popup.publish.title: Title
popup.publish.too-many-processing: You have {{scenes}} scenes processing. You can publish another when one finishes.
popup.render-image.format-tip: PNG: lossless, with transparency. JPEG: small file, no transparency. WebP: smaller than PNG, with transparency. EXR: floating-point image in linear light for compositing.
popup.render-image.level-horizon-tip: Keeps the panorama horizon level and only takes over the viewing direction. Off: the camera tilt is taken over too.
popup.render-image.projection-tip: Standard: a normal camera image. 360°: an all-round panorama from the camera position, e.g. for panorama viewers and VR. Stereo: one panorama per eye, stacked.
popup.render-image.show-debug-overlays-t: Renders helpers such as the grid, camera icons, light gizmos and the selection highlight into the image. Usually off.
popup.render-image.transparent-backgroun: Leaves the background see-through (alpha channel), e.g. for cut-outs or compositing.
popup.render-video.bitrate-tip: Amount of data per second of video: higher means better image quality and a bigger file. High suits most uses.
popup.render-video.codec-tip: H.264 plays almost everywhere. H.265 is smaller at the same quality but does not play everywhere. VP9 and AV1 for WebM. PNG: lossless with alpha.
popup.render-video.compatibility.check-f: Encoder support could not be determined. Try reloading the browser.
popup.render-video.compatibility.option-: Encoder support could not be determined
popup.render-video.compatibility.some-di: Some resolutions are unavailable with {{codec}}, {{frameRate}} fps and {{bitrate}} bitrate on this browser or device.
popup.render-video.compatibility.unavail: Video encoding is not available in this browser.
popup.render-video.compatibility.unsuppo: {{resolution}} with {{codec}}, {{frameRate}} fps and {{bitrate}} bitrate is not supported by this browser or device.
popup.render-video.compatibility.workaro: Try a lower frame rate or bitrate, another compatible codec or format, or update your browser or graphics driver.
popup.render-video.portrait-tip: Swaps width and height, e.g. 1080×1920 for Reels, Shorts and Stories.
popup.shortcuts.copy-key: Drag a Copy of the Key
popup.shortcuts.stamp-key: Overwrite Key with Current Camera Pose
popup.shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
popup.webgpu-unavailable: This export requires WebGPU, which is not available in this browser. Please try a recent version of Chrome, Edge or Safari.
select-toolbar.color-clump-tip: On: selects only the same-coloured splats connected to the clicked one, e.g. a sky-blue blob in a tree. The real sky stays untouched. Off: every matching colour in the whole scene.
select-toolbar.color-radius-tip: Only within this distance of the clicked splat (scene units, usually metres). 0 = no limit.
select-toolbar.color-tolerance-tip: How close the colour must be to the clicked splat: 0 = identical, 1 = any colour. For sky floaters usually 0.1–0.25.
select-toolbar.flood-threshold-tip: How much the opacity of neighbouring pixels may differ from the clicked spot. Low = only equally dense areas, high = the selection spreads further. Default 0.2.
sm.aishots.ai-no-key: Add your own Claude API key in the settings to use Claude.
sm.aishots.ai-offline: Offline – camera moves are suggested without AI.
sm.aishots.anchor-add-tip: Remembers the current view as a favourite angle. Suggested moves pass through or end at these angles. At most 3; the oldest gives way.
sm.aishots.apply-tip: Creates a new shot camera with this move (one undo step).
sm.aishots.capture-tip: Takes the active box or sphere selection, otherwise the bounds of the selected splats, otherwise the whole scene.
sm.aishots.card-preview-tip: Show this move in the viewport (as the preview, to adjust and tidy up)
sm.aishots.disable-loop-tip: Recommended for camera moves. Applies to all cameras.
sm.aishots.distance-none: No object yet – load a scene.
sm.aishots.distance-tip: Camera distance to the centre of the object, in metres (scene units while the scale is unknown). Which point of the move it sets depends on the move (see under “Move”). The ring in the viewport shows it and can be dragged. Also applies to Claude’s suggestions and favourite angles.
sm.aishots.duration-info: {{frames}} frames at {{fps}} fps · fits the timeline ({{timeline}})
sm.aishots.duration-info-long: {{frames}} frames at {{fps}} fps · longer than the timeline ({{timeline}}), “Fit timeline length” extends it
sm.aishots.duration-tip: Length of the move in seconds (at the timeline’s frame rate).
sm.aishots.enable-dof-tip: Needed for the focus pull. Applies to all cameras.
sm.aishots.err.generate: Camera moves could not be suggested.
sm.aishots.err.noObject: No visible splats in the scene.
sm.aishots.err.rate: Rate limit reached – try again shortly.
sm.aishots.generate-tip: Computes six variants with preview stills; with Claude on, Claude plans them from the wish and rates the stills. The live preview needs no click.
sm.aishots.move-info.all: Mixes the moves that suit the camera height; the preview shows the best one.
sm.aishots.move-info.crane: Rises (or sinks) towards the object. Distance = at the end.
sm.aishots.move-info.flyover: Flies over the object at height and tilts down. Distance = at the start.
sm.aishots.move-info.orbit: Circles the object. Distance = radius of the circle.
sm.aishots.move-info.pushIn: Slow approach. Distance = at the start, it ends at about half of it.
sm.aishots.move-info.reveal: Starts close beside the object and pulls back to the full view. Distance = at the end.
sm.aishots.move-info.slide: Lateral track along the object. Distance = closest point of the track.
sm.aishots.move-info.walk: Ego view at eye height above the ground, from waypoint to waypoint at walking pace, with gait bob and handheld shake – for city walks.
sm.aishots.move-tip: Which kind of camera move. “All” mixes the moves that suit the height; one move gives several variants of it (other sides, directions and sweeps).
sm.aishots.object-none: Not set – uses the active box or sphere, the selection or the whole scene.
sm.aishots.preview.apply-tip: Creates a new shot camera with this move (one undo step). Walks bring their gait bob and shake along.
sm.aishots.preview.cleanup-tip: Keeps your rough shape and cleans it: smooth, even speed, object in frame, clear of the geometry – without computing everything anew.
sm.aishots.preview.key-tip: Key at frame {{frame}}: drag horizontally, Shift = up / down
sm.aishots.preview.none: No move yet – load a scene or select an object.
sm.aishots.preview.none-walk: Set at least two waypoints on the ground.
sm.aishots.preview.picking-hint: Click on the ground to add waypoints · Esc ends
sm.aishots.preview.play-tip: Flies the viewport along the move in real time, including gait bob and shake. Esc stops.
sm.aishots.preview.rate-tip: Renders three stills of this move and asks Claude for a rating – only on click; the images are sent to Anthropic.
sm.aishots.preview.reset-tip: Drops hand edits and computes the move from the settings again.
sm.aishots.preview.ring-tip: Distance ring: drag to bring the camera closer or further away
sm.aishots.preview.show-tip: Path, camera at the start and distance ring of the current move, computed live from the settings (without Claude).
sm.aishots.preview.waypoint-tip: Waypoint: drag along the ground, double-click or right-click removes it
sm.aishots.reapply-hint: Suggestions already applied are added again as new cameras.
sm.aishots.score-tip: {{percent}} % – free view and scan data along the path (heuristic).
sm.aishots.set-timeline-tip: Extends the timeline when a move needs more frames.
sm.aishots.settings.get-key: Create an API key at console.anthropic.com
sm.aishots.settings.hint: Claude (Anthropic) only. Your API key stays in your browser: Splatmania sends it only directly to the Anthropic API (api.anthropic.com), never to design4real or any other server. We cannot see, store or log it. Costs are billed to your Anthropic account; we recommend a separate key with a spending limit. Without a key, camera moves are suggested offline without AI.
sm.aishots.settings.remember-hint: Stored in this website’s browser storage – only on your own devices.
sm.aishots.status.waitingVisible: Waiting for the tab to become visible…
sm.aishots.style-info: Camera {{height}} above the ground (bottom of the object)
sm.aishots.style-tip: Where the camera stays during the move. Eye level and frog’s eye keep it near the ground, aerial makes drone shots. Also applies to Claude’s suggestions.
sm.aishots.title: Camera move suggestions
sm.aishots.use-ai-tip: Claude picks moves for the wish and rates the rendered previews. The preview images are sent to Anthropic.
sm.aishots.walk.auto-none: No free walkable area found around the object.
sm.aishots.walk.auto-tip: Suggests a round walk around the object through the free space.
sm.aishots.walk.bob-tip: Up and down per step. Goes into the new camera as a keyable value (camera properties → Walk & handheld).
sm.aishots.walk.clear-tip: Removes all waypoints of the walk-through.
sm.aishots.walk.edit-hint: Drag waypoints in the viewport, a double-click removes one. “Tidy up” finds the way around obstacles.
sm.aishots.walk.eye-tip: Camera height above the detected ground.
sm.aishots.walk.look-tip: How far ahead along the way the view looks: more = calmer turns.
sm.aishots.walk.need-points: Set at least two waypoints (“Set”) or let them be suggested (“Automatic”).
sm.aishots.walk.pick-tip: Click on the ground in the viewport to add waypoints (Esc ends). A click on a wall or a car finds the ground below.
sm.aishots.walk.picking: Click on the ground in the viewport · Esc ends
sm.aishots.walk.route-tip: Searches the way between the waypoints through the free space (where a person can stand) instead of walking straight.
sm.aishots.walk.shake-tip: Random turning and tilting like a camera held in the hand. 0 = steady as on a tripod.
sm.aishots.walk.speed-tip: About 1.3 m/s is a relaxed walk. The duration follows from the length of the way.
sm.aishots.walk.step-tip: Step frequency, about 1.9 Hz at 1.3 m/s.
sm.aishots.walk.unknown-scale: Scale unknown: eye height, pace and bob count 1 scene unit as 1 m. Set the scale under “Object”.
sm.aishots.warn.collision: Path came close to geometry – camera moved outward
sm.aishots.warn.compressed: Move was squeezed to fit the timeline length
sm.aishots.warn.occluded: View of the object partly blocked
sm.aishots.warn.walkBlocked: The way passes through scan geometry – turn on “Find way around obstacles” or move waypoints
sm.aishots.warn.walkNoRoute: No free way found between some waypoints – the walk goes straight there
sm.aishots.wish-placeholder: Wish to Claude, e.g. slow, dramatic reveal from below
sm.align.align-tip: Align all layers with at least 3 point pairs to the reference
sm.align.auto-failed: no matching pose found – the layers may overlap too little. Set anchor points.
sm.align.auto-tip: Aligns every visible layer onto the reference by itself, from any position, rotation and scale (shape and colour are compared, then the fit is refined)
sm.align.clear-tip: Delete all anchor points of the active layer
sm.align.degenerate: The points lie on a line or on top of each other – please spread them as a triangle.
sm.align.help: Auto align finds the position, rotation and scale of every visible layer by itself. If it misses, set anchor points: pick the active layer in the scene manager and click its surface; point n pairs with point n of the reference. Drag = move, right-click = delete.
sm.align.layer-pick-tip: Click to make this layer the active layer, e.g. to place anchor points on it.
sm.align.no-anchors: No layers with anchor points to align.
sm.align.no-hit: No hit on the active layer.
sm.align.no-other: No other visible layer to refine.
sm.align.no-overlap: The layers don't overlap – roughly align them with anchor points first.
sm.align.other-tip: Symmetric or repetitive scenes can fit several ways: switches to the next candidate
sm.align.radius-auto-tip: Measures the overlap of the layers and takes 1/20 of its diagonal
sm.align.radius-hint: Refine bridges an offset of up to {{value}}: it searches that far first, then narrows down. Too small misses the matching surface, too large can snap onto a wrong one.
sm.align.radius-tip: How far apart the layers may still be after the rough alignment. Refine searches this far first, then narrows down. The circle in the view shows the size.
sm.align.refine-tip: Fine alignment on the splat centres (after Auto align or anchor points)
sm.align.scale-tip: Also matches the layer's size to the reference when aligning (uniform scale). Turn off if the scans already share the same scale, e.g. from the same device.
sm.align.title: Align
sm.align.too-few: Too few points in the overlapping area.
sm.anim.delete-key-tip: Delete the key at the current frame
sm.anim.display-tip: This layer's display mode, overrides the global mode
sm.anim.fade-duration-tip: Length of Fade in / Fade out in frames.
sm.anim.interpolation-tip: How values move between two keys: Linear at an even pace, Smooth eases in and out.
sm.anim.mix-tip: Blend splat (0) ↔ point cloud (1), animatable. Off = follows the display mode
sm.anim.opacity-tip: The layer's opacity. With keys it animates over time
sm.anim.set-key-tip: Store opacity, point mix and transform at the current frame
sm.anim.splat-size-tip: Own splat size for this object (tick to enable). Off = the global size from Display. Display only, the splat data stays unchanged
sm.anim.title: Layer animation
sm.background.colors-tip: Colour at the top of the sky, at the horizon and below the horizon.
sm.background.spread-tip: Angle above the horizon where the sky reaches its top colour. Small = short, strong band at the horizon; large = slow gradient.
sm.background.tip: Background of the viewport and of every export: a plain colour (the first colour above) or a sky gradient from the horizon up. The gradient follows the real horizon, also in 360° exports. Transparent exports stay transparent.
sm.background.title: Background
sm.camera-props.fov-tip: Field of view in degrees (long side of the image)
sm.camera-props.ipd-tip: Stereo eye separation in scene units (6.4 cm in a metric scene). Larger = stronger depth
sm.camera-props.lens-tip: Focal length in mm (full-frame equivalent) and the field of view it gives, in degrees
sm.camera-props.position-tip: Camera position. Moving it keeps the viewing direction
sm.camera-props.projection-tip: What this camera renders in image and video exports: a normal lens image, a 360° panorama, or a stereo 360° for VR headsets (top/bottom). The export dialogs take it over
sm.camera-props.target-row-tip: The camera’s look-at target: click to move it with the move tool and key it separately
sm.camera-props.target-tip: The point the camera looks at. It has its own keys: animate it separately from the camera position, e.g. to pan across the scene while the camera drives.
sm.camera-props.title: Selected camera
sm.camera-props.to-view-tip: Put the camera where the viewport is looking
sm.cameras.edit-path-tip: Drag the selected camera's keys in the viewport (position and target); Shift-click the path to insert a key
sm.cameras.fade-tip: Cross-fade at the cut under the playhead, in frames. Applies to video exports with the "Cut" camera; the viewport cuts hard.
sm.cameras.frustums-tip: Shows the cameras in the viewport: camera icon, keys and look-at target. Off hides all camera guides, paths included.
sm.cameras.mode.camera-tip: The viewport looks through the selected camera (K)
sm.cameras.mode.cut-tip: The viewport follows the cut track
sm.cameras.mode.free-tip: Free editor camera: the timeline does not move the viewport
sm.cameras.paths-tip: Shows each camera's flight path as a dashed line once it has several keys.
sm.cameras.remove-selected: Remove the selected camera (the last camera keeps existing, its keys are removed)
sm.cameras.title: Cameras
sm.cleanup.adaptive-tip: Adaptive distribution (more detail where it matters) instead of a uniform rate
sm.cleanup.cluster-min-tip: How much a splat must contribute to the cluster to stay (default 0.1). Higher finds more splats at the edges.
sm.cleanup.cluster-opacity-tip: Opacity from which a grid cube counts as solid (default 0.999). Lower lets thin areas join the cluster too.
sm.cleanup.cluster-res-tip: Size of the coarse grid cubes in scene units (default 1). Larger joins parts across gaps, smaller separates more precisely.
sm.cleanup.cluster-voxel-tip: Coarse voxel size, opacity threshold, minimum contribution
sm.cleanup.count-tip: Exact target number of splats. 0 = use the percentage.
sm.cleanup.delete-now-tip: Off: affected splats are only selected (then press Delete). On: delete right away (undoable)
sm.cleanup.find-floaters-tip: Splats that don't contribute to any solid voxel (GPU)
sm.cleanup.find-outside-tip: Everything outside the connected cluster at the seed (GPU)
sm.cleanup.floaters-voxel-tip: Voxel size (world units), opacity threshold of solid voxels, minimum contribution
sm.cleanup.needs-webgpu: This function needs WebGPU (GPU voxelization). Please use a browser with WebGPU.
sm.cleanup.run-decimate-tip: Simplifies the layer into a new layer; the original is hidden
sm.cleanup.seed-focus-tip: Set the seed to the camera's focus point (e.g. after double-clicking into the scene)
sm.cleanup.seed-pivot-tip: Set the seed to the pivot position (transform gizmo or pick)
sm.cleanup.seed-tip: Start point of the cluster in world coordinates
sm.cleanup.title: Clean up
sm.compose.align.scale-tip: Also matches the size of the scans when aligning (uniform scale). Usually not needed for scans from the same device.
sm.compose.areas.revert-all-tip: Brings back the splats of all deleted blurry areas.
sm.compose.card.accept-tip: Hides the coarser scan's splats in this area (not deleted). "Revert" or Ctrl+Z brings them back.
sm.compose.card.reject-tip: Discards the suggestion; nothing is hidden. It stays rejected after a new analysis too; "Offer again" brings it back.
sm.compose.suggest.accept-ticked-tip: Accepts all ticked suggestions at once: the coarser splats there are hidden, not deleted.
sm.compose.suggest.revert-all-tip: Shows again everything that accepted suggestions hid. Splats hidden by hand stay hidden.
sm.compose.view.colors-tip: Tints each scan in its own colour so it is clear which part belongs to which scan. Display only.
sm.compose.view.markers-tip: In the "Suggestions" step, shows every suggestion and every blurry area as a numbered marker in the view. Click a marker to open its card. Display only.
sm.compose.view.zones-tip: Shows the transition zones between the scans: as markers in the view with the measured offset at the seam, and as a list under each scan. Click a marker to fly there. Display only.
sm.dof.enabled-tip: Turns depth of field on or off. Applies to all cameras; each camera sets its own focus and aperture.
sm.export.active-layer-tip: Exports only the currently selected splat layer instead of all visible layers.
sm.floaters.accept-tip: Take this group into the selection
sm.floaters.find-tip: Search the selected layer for floaters and select them; nothing is deleted

sm.compose.suggest.tick-all-tip: Ticks or unticks every open area for “Accept ticked”, the folded smaller ones too. Large-area ones keep their own tick.

sm.compose.areas.failed: The search for blurry areas failed – the detailed comparison is below.

sm.compose.areas.deleted-tip: deleted – revert or Ctrl+Z to compare

sm.compose.details.tip: The detailed suggestions, cell by cell: where one scan is finer than the other and covers it. Rarely needed.
sm.compose.card.pick-tip: Click the card: the camera flies to this spot
sm.compose.card.effect: Hides {{n}} splats of {{l}} · {{k}} stay where {{w}} has nothing nearby
sm.compose.card.effect-haze: Hides {{n}} splats of {{l}} (incl. {{m}} blurry haze splats) · {{k}} stay where {{w}} has nothing nearby

sm.compose.card.accepted-tip: accepted – revert it or press Ctrl+Z to compare
sm.compose.card.hand-tip: This suggestion's splats are already hidden – by hand or with another tool. There is nothing left to accept, and “Before” would show a hole.

sm.compose.check.density-forced: Not sparser: {{f}}× as many splats per area, but cell by cell mostly only {{c}}×
sm.compose.check.texture-forced: Colour detail: {{f}}× ({{l}} {{tl}} %, {{w}} {{tw}} %), but cell by cell mostly only {{c}}×

sm.compose.skip.force-apart: The scans lie too far apart there – this cannot become a suggestion.
sm.compose.view.map-tip: Colours every cell in the colour of the scan that is clearly finer there (pale: somewhat finer, grey: about equally fine). Display only.
sm.compose.view.hidden-tip: Hidden splats disappear entirely in the scan composition instead of staying faintly visible – including the ones you hid yourself. Display only.

sm.depth.enabled-tip: Rect, lasso, polygon, brush and click only pick splats inside the depth range
sm.depth.min-alpha-tip: Visible splats only: with depth selection on, a splat only wins a pixel if it contributes at least this opacity there. 0 = off
sm.depth.near-tip: Minimum distance from the camera (view depth of the splat centre)
sm.depth.outside-tip: How splats outside the range are displayed
sm.depth.title: Depth filter
sm.depthmap.enabled-tip: Also saves a 16-bit greyscale depth map (<name>_depth.png), e.g. for ControlNet, After Effects or tools without EXR. Image sequences get one per frame.
sm.depthmap.far-tip: Distance that becomes the far end of the grey scale. Everything further and the empty background count as far.
sm.depthmap.near-tip: Distance that becomes the near end of the grey scale (scene units, metres in a metric scan).

sm.depthmap.range-tip: How distances spread over the grey scale. Automatic takes the visible scan without the empty background and stray floaters; a sequence keeps the range of its first frame. By hand: a small room e.g. 0.5–8, a large square 2–200.
sm.display.softness-tip: Screen-space blur added to every splat, in px² (0.3 = 3DGS standard). Lower = sharper, but fine detail may flicker or alias
sm.display.splat-size-tip: Scales every splat for display and rendering (1 = as trained). Objects can override it under Layer animation. Smaller = crisper, gaps may open. The splat data and exports stay unchanged

sm.dof.aperture-tip: Lens radius: larger = shallower depth of field
sm.dof.focus-tip: Distance of the focal plane from the camera
sm.dof.max-blur-tip: Upper limit of the blur in pixels
sm.dof.pick-tip: Click in the viewport to focus on the surface under the cursor

sm.gait.shake-rate-tip: How fast the handheld shake moves.
sm.gait.shake-tip: Handheld shake: random turning and tilting in degrees (0 = off).
sm.gait.step-rate-tip: Step frequency in Hz: about 1.8–2 steps per second at walking pace.

sm.help._overview.intro: Splatmania adds tools for camera moves, animation, look and export to the splat editor. Here you find a short guide for each tool.
sm.help._overview.title: Splatmania tools
sm.help.aiShots.intro: Suggests ready-made camera moves such as orbit, push-in or crane for an object. You apply a move as a new camera with one click.
sm.help.aiShots.steps:
Open “Camera move suggestions” in the right toolbar.
Click “Use object”: it takes the active box or sphere selection, otherwise the selected splats, otherwise the whole scene.
Frame a nice view and click “Remember angle” (at most 3) so the moves pass through these angles.
Set “Duration (s)” and “Distance”: the distance is in metres (scene units while the scale is unknown) and as a multiple of the object size. The viewport shows the path, the start camera and the distance ring at once; drag the ring to change the distance.
Drag the path’s keys roughly into shape and click “Tidy up”: smoothed, even speed, object in frame, clear of the geometry. “▶ Test drive” flies the move in the viewport.
To use Claude, click “Settings”, enter your own “API key” in the “AI (Claude)” section, click “Save & test”, then write your “Wish to Claude”.
Click “Suggest camera moves” and look at the previews.
Click “Apply” on a move, or tick several and click “Apply selected”; below you find “Fit timeline length”, “Turn off timeline loop” and “Turn on depth of field”.
For a “Walk-through (pedestrian)”, pick it under “Move”, click “Set” and click waypoints on the ground (or “Automatic”); set eye height, pace, gait bob and handheld shake, then “Apply as camera”.
sm.help.aiShots.tips:
Without a key or offline, moves are suggested without AI.
With “Use Claude” on, the preview images are sent to Anthropic; costs are billed to your Anthropic account.
Each applied move becomes a new camera and can be undone in one step.
Pick a “Camera height” (eye level, frog’s eye, raised, aerial) and a “Move” to steer the suggestions; one move gives several variants of it.
Scale: XGRIDS / PortalCam scans (LCC) are metric; for Postshot and other PLYs set “Scale” (e.g. from the real object height), otherwise lengths stay scene units.
Gait bob and handheld shake belong to the camera: in its properties under “Walk & handheld” every value can be keyed; preview, playback and video export include them.
sm.help.aiShots.title: Camera move suggestions
sm.help.align.intro: Lines up several scans of the same scene. Auto align does it by itself; anchor points are the manual way.
sm.help.align.steps:
Open the align tool in the right toolbar (J key).
Use “Reference” to pick the layer that stays fixed.
Click “Auto align”: every visible layer is placed onto the reference, from any position, rotation and size.
If a layer says “please check”, try “Other solution” or set anchor points: click at least three distinct spots on the reference, then the same spots in the same order on the other layer, and click “Align”.
Finish with “Refine”. “Max. offset” says how far apart the layers may still be; Auto measures it, and the circle in the view shows the size.
sm.help.align.tips:
Drag a point to move it, right-click to delete it; “Clear points” removes all points of the active layer.
The depth filter also hides floaters while you set points.
To put several scans together at their transition zones, use the Scan composition.
sm.help.align.title: Align (anchor points)
sm.help.cameras.intro: In the scene manager you create as many shot cameras as you like, animate them with keys and cut them together on the cut track.
sm.help.cameras.steps:
In the scene list, use + next to “Cameras” to add a camera, ⧉ to duplicate the selected one and − to delete it.
Under “View & cut”, pick the “Viewport” mode: “Free”, “Look through” (K key) or “Cut”.
Move to a frame on the timeline, set up the view and press “Add Key” or Enter to key the selected camera.
Drag in an empty area of the cut track to create a shot of the selected camera; drag its edges to trim it, right-click to switch camera or delete it.
With “✎ Edit path (X)” you drag the keys directly in the viewport; Shift-click the path to insert a key.
Under “Selected camera”, choose the “Projection”: “Normal”, “360°” or “360° VR”, and set the “Lens”.
Turn on “Depth of field”, click “Pick focus” and then the surface that should be sharp; “Focus” and “Aperture” can be keyed.
sm.help.cameras.tips:
“Cross-fade” at a cut only applies to video exports with the “Cut” camera; the viewport cuts hard.
Changes that are not keyed are lost when the frame changes: an orange key button shows this.
The camera’s target is its own object: click “Target” under the camera in the scene list, move it with the move tool and key it on its own.
sm.help.cameras.title: Cameras
sm.help.cleanup.intro: Finds floaters (stray splats, detached clumps and fog in the air), splats outside the main object and invalid splats, and simplifies large layers. It works on the selected layer.
sm.help.cleanup.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Clean up” in its properties.
Under “Find floaters”, set the strictness and click “Find floaters”: the floaters are selected and listed in groups.
Click a group to fly to it, untick groups that are real objects, or let “Check with Claude” sort them out.
Delete the rest with “Delete selection” (undoable).
Under “Keep cluster”, set the seed on the object with “Seed = pivot” or “Seed = focus” and click “Find outside”.
Under “Invalid splats (NaN)”, click “NaN splats” to find broken splats.
To simplify, set “Keep %” under “Decimate (new layer)” and click “Run decimate”.
sm.help.cleanup.tips:
The floater search runs in the background and needs no WebGPU; changing the strictness needs no new search.
“Check with Claude” only appears with an API key in the settings and sends small rendered images, never the scan.
The cluster search needs a browser with WebGPU. Decimate creates a new layer and only hides the original.
sm.help.cleanup.title: Clean up
sm.help.compose.intro: Puts 2–4 scans of one place together, step by step: every scan is aligned where it overlaps the others, so the seams sit tight even when the scanner drifted.
sm.help.compose.steps:
Load the scans (File › Import) and open Scan composition in the right toolbar.
Step 1: tick the scans (2–4). The overlap is measured, and the scan that shares the most becomes the suggested reference.
Step 2: click “Align automatically”. Every scan is attached to the placed ones; the panel lists its transition zones with the remaining offset.
Hover a zone to see its outline, ⌖ flies there. “Align here” fits the scan at another zone.
If a scan says “no reliable fit”, correct it with anchor points and align again.
Step 3: click “Analyse”. The scans are compared cell by cell; “Map” colours where each scan is clearly finer, and a double-click in the view shows the numbers at that spot.
Step 4: each suggestion replaces the coarser version of an area with the finer one. Compare with “Before” and “After”, then “Accept” or “Reject”. The coarser scan's splats are only hidden, not deleted.
Step 6: "Merge" turns the scans into one layer without the hidden splats (deleted areas, accepted suggestions). The originals are hidden; export afterwards.
sm.help.compose.tips:
“Colour scans” shows which scan is where; “One at a time” shows them one by one.
The whole alignment is one undo step.
Offsets: green under 1 cm, orange up to 3 cm, red above (in metric scenes).
“Accept” and “Accept ticked” are one undo step each (Ctrl+Z); “Revert” shows the splats again.
“Hidden gone” removes hidden splats from view entirely in the wizard; “Map” and the previews are display only.
Image and video renders show the scene as it is: without “Colour scans”, “Map”, previews and “Hidden gone”, unless “Show Debug Overlays” is on.
sm.help.compose.title: Scan composition
sm.help.depthFilter.intro: Limits selection and picking to a depth range in front of the camera. That way you can grab floaters in front of a wall, or the wall behind them.
sm.help.depthFilter.steps:
In the floating “Depth filter” panel, switch on the toggle in the title bar.
Set the distance range from the camera with “Near (m)” and “Far (m)”.
Under “Outside”, choose how splats outside the range appear: “Normal”, “Dim” or “Hide”.
Now select with rectangle, lasso, polygon, brush or click; only splats inside the range are picked.
With “Selection Depth” on in the bottom toolbar (N key), “Min. opacity” sets how opaque a splat must be to be hit.
sm.help.depthFilter.tips:
The filter has no effect on sphere and box selection.
What counts is the centre of a splat; the metres are scene units.
sm.help.depthFilter.title: Depth filter
sm.help.export.intro: Renders your camera moves as a video, a 360° panorama or a stereo 360° for VR headsets, frame by frame at full quality.
sm.help.export.steps:
In the “Render” menu, open “Video” (for stills and panoramas, “Image”).
Under “Camera”, choose “Cut (one MP4)”, a single camera or “All cameras separately”.
Under “Projection”, choose “Standard”, “360° Equirectangular” or “360° Stereo (top/bottom)”.
For stereo, set “Eye distance”, “Pole fade from” and “Stereo quality”.
Set “Resolution”, “Format”, “Frame Rate” and, if wanted, “Motion blur”.
Click “Render” and wait until all frames are done.
sm.help.export.tips:
A camera’s projection from its properties is preselected in the dialog.
Stereo 360° takes much longer; “Draft (48 segments)” is good for a quick test.
“Open in player / VR” in the “Render” menu shows the scene right away in the player with a VR button.
“Depth map (greyscale)” saves a 16-bit depth image next to the picture; set the depth range automatically or by hand (small room e.g. 0.5–8, large square 2–200).
sm.help.export.title: Video, 360° and VR export
sm.help.layerAnim.intro: Animates the opacity, position and display of a single splat layer over time, for example a fade in or out.
sm.help.layerAnim.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Layer animation” in its properties.
Move to a frame on the timeline, set the “Opacity” or the transform and click “◆ Set key”.
Repeat at another frame; the values blend automatically in between.
For a quick fade, click “Fade in” or “Fade out” from the current frame.
Under “Interpolation”, choose a linear or smooth curve.
“Point mix” blends the layer smoothly between splats and points, “Display” overrides the global mode.
sm.help.layerAnim.tips:
In the layer row of the timeline: double-click sets a key, drag moves it, right-click deletes it.
Opacity applies per splat: dense layers only fade visibly towards the end.
sm.help.layerAnim.title: Layer animation
sm.help.light.intro: Relights a scan: you dim the captured light and add up to four lights of your own, for example for a night scene.
sm.help.light.steps:
Open “Light” in the right toolbar and keep “Light on” switched on.
Lower “Scanned light” to darken the scene, and add base light with “Ambient” and “Ambient colour”.
Add a light with “+ Sun”, “+ Lamp” or “+ Spot”.
For the sun, set “Direction (°)” and “Height (°)”.
Place a lamp or spot with “Place” (click the model) or “At camera”; aim a spot at a point with “Aim”.
Adjust “Colour”, “Intensity”, “Range”, “Cone (°)” and “Softness”.
Use the key button in the panel header to set a key when the light should animate.
sm.help.light.tips:
New light brightens and tints, it cannot remove shadows that were captured.
Esc cancels placing.
The lights are not included in the player/VR export.
Lights also appear in the scene list under “Lights”: click one to move it with the arrows in the viewport, the cross or Delete removes it.
sm.help.light.title: Light
sm.help.look.intro: Gives the whole scene a film look with glow, grading, lens effects, fog and a colour LUT. The look applies in the viewport and in every export; the splat data is not changed.
sm.help.look.steps:
Open “Look” in the right toolbar and turn on “Look on”.
Under “Glow”, make bright areas glow with “Strength”, “Threshold”, “Radius” and “Glow colour”.
Under “Grading”, set “Exposure”, “Contrast”, “Saturation” and “Temperature”.
Under “Lens”, add “Vignette”, “Film grain” and “Chromatic aberration” if you like.
Hide ragged edges with “Fog”: “Strength”, “Start (m)” and “End (m)”.
Under “Colour LUT”, click “Load…” to pick a .cube file and adjust the “LUT strength”.
Use the ◇ key button in the panel header to set a key when the look should change over time.
sm.help.look.tips:
Vignette and chromatic aberration are not applied to 360° panoramas.
The player/VR export only approximates the look; grain, LUT and fog are missing there.
sm.help.look.title: Look
sm.help.pointCloud.intro: Sets how splats are drawn: as splats or as a point cloud, plus size and softness. This only affects display and rendering, not the splat data.
sm.help.pointCloud.steps:
Open “Display” in the properties of a splat.
Under “Mode”, choose “Splats” or “Point cloud”.
Adjust “Splat size” and “Softness”: smaller or lower looks crisper.
For the point cloud, set “Point size” and “Colour” (“Original” or “Uniform”).
Under “Advanced”, set “Size in” to “Pixels” or “World” and give the points some “Glow”.
sm.help.pointCloud.tips:
Single layers can override the mode under “Layer animation” → “Display”.
The mode also applies to the video export.
sm.help.pointCloud.title: Display
sm.help.quality.intro: Shows where a scan is blurry or weak and, with several scans, finds which one is sharper where. You can then select and delete the weak splats.
sm.help.quality.steps:
Open the quality tool in the right toolbar (U key).
Click “Compute scores”; under “Display”, the heatmap shows the weakest areas.
Set the “Threshold” and click “Select below threshold”.
With two or more visible scans, click “Compare scans” and adjust “Grid” and “Tolerance” if needed.
Click “Select worse” to pick splats that are sharper in another scan.
Delete the selection with Delete.
sm.help.quality.tips:
The heatmap is relative: it only shows the weakest areas of this one scan.
Compute the scores again after deleting.
The depth filter does not apply to “Select below threshold”.
Image and video renders show the scene without the heatmap, unless “Show Debug Overlays” is on.
sm.help.quality.title: Quality
sm.help.section.intro: Cuts the model from the top down, for example to remove the roof of a house down to the floor plan. Nothing is deleted, and the cut can be animated.
sm.help.section.steps:
Open the section tool in the right toolbar (Y key).
Drag the “Cut” slider: 0 % cuts nothing, 100 % cuts down to the floor plan height; or type the “Height (m)”.
If needed, use “Pick floor” and a click to set the floor height, and adjust the “Floor plan”.
Under “Applies to”, choose “All visible” or “Active layer”, and under “Edge”, “Soft” or “Hard”.
Turn on “Show plane” to see the cut height as a grid.
Use the key button next to the slider at different frames to animate the cut.
For an export without the roof, click “Select cut-off splats” and press Delete.
sm.help.section.tips:
“Re-measure” finds the top and bottom again, for example after deleting floaters.
The grid only shows in the editor, never in exports.
sm.help.section.title: Section
sm.help.titles.intro: Puts text over the image, for example a title, a place name or credits. It shows in the viewport and in image and video exports.
sm.help.titles.steps:
Open “Titles” in the right toolbar.
Move to the start frame on the timeline and click “+ Add title at current frame”.
Type the text and set the frame range with “Start at the current frame” and “End at the current frame”.
Set “Fade (s)” for fading in and out.
Choose “Position”, “Align”, “Size (%)”, “Font” and “Colour”, plus “Bold” and “Box” if needed.
“Show” jumps to the title, “Delete” removes it.
sm.help.titles.tips: Titles are not drawn into 360° exports.
sm.help.titles.title: Titles
sm.help.transitions.intro: Makes a layer appear or disappear with an effect, for example a glowing materialize from particles.
sm.help.transitions.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Transitions” in its properties.
Click “+ In” for a build-up or “+ Out” for a tear-down from the current frame; or Shift-drag (Shift+Alt-drag) in the layer row of the timeline.
Pick the effect: Sweep, Radial, Dissolve, Grow, Fly-in or Wave.
Set “Start / length”, “Easing”, “Direction” and “Origin”.
Fine-tune under “Advanced”, for example “Edge”, “Glow edge”, “Glow colour”, “Scatter” and “Swirl”.
Drag the block on the timeline or drag its ends; right-click or “Delete transition” removes it.
sm.help.transitions.tips:
For even phases in a dissolve, linear easing works best.
Before an in transition the layer is invisible, after an out transition it is gone.
Selection and picking always see the splats at their final position.
sm.help.transitions.title: Transitions
sm.image.depth-tip: Adds a Z channel with the camera distance per pixel (scene units, empty = 1e10). Colour is written in linear light.
sm.key.animated: Animated. Click to set a key at this frame
sm.key.changed: Changed but not keyed: the change is lost when the frame changes. Click to key it
sm.key.keyed: Key at this frame. Click to remove it
sm.key.static: Not animated. Click to set a key here and start animating this property
sm.light.add-from-list: Add a light in the light panel
sm.light.add-point-tip: A lamp that shines from one point in all directions, like a light bulb. Appears just in front of the camera.
sm.light.add-spot-tip: A cone of light in one direction, like a spotlight. Starts at the camera and points where it looks.
sm.light.add-sun-tip: Parallel light from one direction, like sunlight. Set direction and height afterwards.
sm.light.aim-tip: Click the model to aim the spot at that point.
sm.light.ambient-tip: Even light from all sides, e.g. a blue night sky after lowering the scanned light.
sm.light.azimuth-tip: Compass direction the sun shines from.
sm.light.baked-tip: How much of the light captured in the scan stays. 1 = as scanned, lower = darker (e.g. for night), then add your own lights.
sm.light.cone-tip: Half opening angle of the spot.
sm.light.elevation-tip: Height of the sun above the horizon. Low values give long grazing light.
sm.light.empty: Add up to four lights. The scan's own light stays baked into its colours: new light brightens and tints it, it cannot remove shadows that were captured.
sm.light.enabled-tip: Switches the added light off without losing it, to compare with the scan as captured.
sm.light.intensity-tip: Brightness of the light. Values above 4 can be typed in.
sm.light.picking: Click the model to place the light (Esc cancels).
sm.light.place-tip: Click the model to put the light just in front of that spot.
sm.light.props-hint: Drag the arrows in the viewport to move the light (the sun: its handle sets the direction). Delete removes it, Ctrl+Z undoes.
sm.light.range-tip: Distance (scene units) at which the light has faded out completely.
sm.light.title: Light
sm.light.to-camera-tip: Moves the light to the current view (a spot then shines where the camera looks).
sm.light.toggle-tip: Switch this light on or off
sm.light.wrap-tip: Lets the light wrap around surfaces. Higher values hide noisy surface directions of real scans.
sm.look.aberration-tip: Red and blue edges toward the corners, like a cheap lens. Not applied to 360° panoramas.
sm.look.bloom-tip: How strongly bright areas glow into their surroundings (bloom). 0 = off.
sm.look.contrast-tip: 1 = unchanged. Higher spreads darks and lights apart, lower flattens the image.
sm.look.enabled-tip: Switch the whole look on or off to compare. It applies in the viewport and in every image, video and 360° export; the splat data is not changed.
sm.look.exposure-tip: Brightness in stops: +1 doubles the light, −1 halves it.
sm.look.fog-color-tip: Off: far splats fade out into the background (also works with transparent exports). On: they take on the fog colour, like haze.
sm.look.fog-end-tip: Distance from the camera where the fog reaches full strength.
sm.look.fog-start-tip: Distance from the camera where the fog begins, in scene units (metres for most scans).
sm.look.fog-strength-tip: Distance fog: splats further away fade into the background (or into the fog colour). Great for hiding the ragged far edges of a scan. 0 = off.
sm.look.grain-tip: Fine noise like film grain; it changes every frame in videos. Also hides banding in soft gradients.
sm.look.lut-strength-tip: Blends between the image without (0) and with the LUT (1).
sm.look.lut-tip: Load a 3D LUT (.cube) from DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Photoshop or a LUT pack to apply its colour look. It is saved with the project.
sm.look.radius-tip: How far the glow spreads: small = tight halo, large = wide haze.
sm.look.reset: Reset the look (keeps it switched on)
sm.look.saturation-tip: 1 = unchanged, 0 = black and white, 2 = very colourful.
sm.look.softness-tip: How gradually the vignette fades in from the centre.
sm.look.threshold-tip: Only areas brighter than this glow. Lower values let more of the scene glow (dreamy, soft); higher values keep the glow to highlights.
sm.look.tint-tip: Tints the glow. White keeps the colours of the glowing areas.
sm.look.title: Look
sm.look.vignette-tip: Darkens the corners of the frame. Not applied to 360° panoramas (they have no frame).
sm.motion-blur.shutter-tip: Share of the frame time the shutter is open: 0.5 is the classic 180° film shutter, 1 blurs the most.
sm.motion-blur.tip: Renders several in-between images per frame and averages them, so fast camera moves and animations blur like on a real camera. Takes as many times longer as there are sub-frames.
sm.motion-blur.title: Motion blur
sm.objects.title: Scene
sm.pano-preview.label: 360° preview · {{camera}} (equirectangular, as exported)
sm.pano-preview.label-stereo: 360° VR preview · {{camera}} (one eye, mono; the export is top/bottom stereo)
sm.pano.north-tip: Off: the panorama centre follows the camera's (or key's) view direction. On: the centre always faces world -Z
sm.pano.source-tip: Where the panorama comes from. For several panoramas you pick a folder
sm.path.handle-tip: Bezier handle: drag to shape the path (Alt moves it on its own), double-click returns to the automatic curve
sm.path.handles-hint: Handles: drag to shape the curve · Alt = break · double-click = auto
sm.path.hint: Drag a key or use the gizmo · Alt = position + target · Shift-click the path = insert key · Delete = remove · F = focus
sm.player.open-tip: Opens the scene in the web player in a new tab, with buttons for VR and AR headsets.
sm.points.color-tip: Original: each point in its splat's colour. Uniform: all points in the colour on the right.
sm.points.mode-tip: Global render mode, also applies to the video export
sm.points.opacity-tip: Opacity of the points in point cloud display.
sm.points.size-in-tip: Pixels: constant on screen. World: gets smaller with distance
sm.points.size-tip: Point diameter in pixels or world units
sm.points.title: Point cloud
sm.properties.empty: Select a splat or a camera in the scene list to see its properties.
sm.properties.title: Properties
sm.quality.compare-scans-tip: Find the sharpest layer per voxel and mark worse splats
sm.quality.compute-tip: Compute the quality score for all visible layers
sm.quality.display-tip: The heatmap is relative: it shows the weakest areas of this scan. Whether one scan is sharper than another in a spot is shown by the comparison.
sm.quality.grid-tip: Comparison grid (voxel size, world units); 0 = automatic from the splat density
sm.quality.heatmap-hint: The heatmap is relative (weakest areas of this scan). Which scan is sharper where: "Compare scans".
sm.quality.mode-compare-tip: Colours the splats red that another scan has sharper at the same spot. Run "Compare scans" first. Display only.
sm.quality.mode-heatmap-tip: Colours each splat by its score: red = weak, yellow = medium, green = good. Run "Compute scores" first. Display only.
sm.quality.mode-threshold-tip: Colours only the splats red whose score is below the threshold, i.e. what "Select below threshold" would pick. Display only.
sm.quality.need-two: The comparison needs at least two visible layers.
sm.quality.no-compare: The active layer has no comparison yet.
sm.quality.no-core: The score core is not connected yet.
sm.quality.no-scores: The active layer has no scores yet.
sm.quality.select-below-tip: Select splats of the active layer below the threshold (then press Delete)
sm.quality.select-worse-tip: Select splats of the active layer that are sharper in another scan
sm.quality.threshold-tip: Score limit from 0 (bad) to 1 (good): splats below it count as weak. Default 0.3.
sm.quality.title: Quality
sm.quality.tolerance-tip: How much worse a layer has to be to get marked
sm.render.no-keys: The selected camera has no keys.
sm.scale.object-height-tip: Enter the real height of the object (e.g. 8 m for a house): the scale follows from it.
sm.scale.tip: How long one scene unit is. XGRIDS / PortalCam scans (LCC) are metric; Postshot and many PLY exports have an arbitrary size. Lengths are shown in metres only when the scale is known.
sm.scale.title: Scale
sm.scale.unit-is-tip: How many metres one scene unit is long. All lengths then show in metres.
sm.scale.unknown-hint: Scale unknown: lengths are scene units, not metres (Postshot scans, for example, have an arbitrary size). Set the scale to see metres.
sm.section.axis-tip: World Y or the active layer's up axis (follows the orient tool)
sm.section.cut-tip: 0 % = nothing cut off, 100 % = down to the floor plan height above the floor
sm.section.edge-tip: Soft: the last centimetres fade out; hard: crisp cut
sm.section.floor-plan-tip: How much of the walls remains at 100 % (above the floor)
sm.section.height-tip: Absolute cut height along the axis, linked to the slider
sm.section.key-tip: Store the cut value at the current frame as a key
sm.section.measure-tip: Determine the top and bottom again from the visible splats
sm.section.pick-floor-tip: The next click in the viewport sets the floor height
sm.section.select-cut-tip: Select the cut-off splats of the active layer (then press Delete)
sm.section.show-plane-tip: Cut plane as a grid (editor only)
sm.section.title: Section
sm.splats.remove-tip: Remove this splat from the scene. This cannot be undone.
sm.splats.title: Splats
sm.splats.visibility-tip: Show or hide this splat in the viewport.
sm.stereo.ipd-tip: IPD in scene units: 0.064 = 6.4 cm in a scene in metres. Unscaled PLYs may use other units; adjust then (larger = stronger 3D effect)
sm.stereo.pole-tip: From this elevation (degrees above/below the horizon) the stereo fades softly into the mono panorama, so there are no double images at the top and bottom
sm.stereo.quality-tip: Number of azimuth strips per eye: more = cleaner disparity, longer render time
sm.stereo.quality-tip-video: Azimuth strips per eye: more = cleaner disparity, longer render time (6 + 2 × segments render passes per frame)
sm.timeline.auto-key-tip: Auto key: every property you change is keyed at the current frame right away (cameras, splats, section)
sm.timeline.camera-row-tip: Click = select the camera and jump to this frame, drag a key = move it, right-click a key = delete it
sm.timeline.channel-row-tip: Keys of this property only: click = jump to this frame, drag a key = move it, right-click a key = delete it
sm.timeline.cut-here-tip: Cut to this camera at the playhead
sm.timeline.cut-tip: Cut track: click a shot = go there, drag a shot's edge = shorten / lengthen it (the cut point moves), right-click = switch camera or delete. Drag in an empty area = new shot of the selected camera
sm.timeline.key-tip: The key button keys the listed properties of the selected camera or splat, plus every changed, not yet keyed value
sm.timeline.layer-tip: double-click = set key, drag a key = move, right-click a key = delete
sm.timeline.light-tip: Light track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.live-tip: Shown by the cut at the playhead
sm.timeline.look-tip: Look track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.section-tip: Section track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.shot-tip: Drag the edges to trim, right-click to switch camera or delete
sm.timeline.transition-tip: {{kind}} transition {{effect}}: frame {{start}}–{{end}} (drag = move, ends = length, right-click = delete)
sm.titles.box-tip: A dark box behind the text instead of a shadow, so it stays readable on bright backgrounds.
sm.titles.empty: Text over the image for a frame range, e.g. a title, a place name or credits. Shown in the viewport and drawn into image and video exports (not 360°).
sm.titles.fade-tip: Length of the fade in and out in seconds. 0 = the title appears and disappears instantly.
sm.titles.frames-tip: First and last frame in which the title is visible. The arrow buttons take the current timeline frame.
sm.titles.jump-tip: Jumps the timeline to the middle of this title.
sm.titles.pos-lower-tip: In the lower third of the image, the usual place for names and locations.
sm.titles.size-tip: Text height as a percentage of the image height, so the title fits any export resolution.
sm.titles.title: Titles
sm.toolbar.aishots-tip: Suggests camera moves around an object automatically and adds them as cameras.
sm.toolbar.appearance-tip: Sets how splats, center points, rings and the selection are shown in the editor.
sm.toolbar.eyedropper-tip: Click a color to select all splats of a similar color, optionally only the connected clump.
sm.toolbar.flood-tip: Selects the connected screen area around the click with similar opacity, e.g. a cloud against empty background.
sm.toolbar.fly-tip: Move freely through the scene with W, A, S, D (Q/E for down/up), good for rooms.
sm.toolbar.footprint-tip: Off: a splat only counts when its center lies inside the selection. On: as soon as its visible area touches the selection.
sm.toolbar.frame-selection-tip: Aims the camera so that the selection fills the view.
sm.toolbar.group-hold-tip: Press and hold for more tools.
sm.toolbar.light-tip: Relights the scene afterwards with custom light sources.
sm.toolbar.local-space-tip: On: the gizmo follows the object's axes. Off: it uses the world axes.
sm.toolbar.look-tip: Look of the whole scene: glow, color grading, lens effects and fog.
sm.toolbar.orbit-tip: The camera circles around a center point, good for looking at an object.
sm.toolbar.orient-tip: Place three points on a surface, e.g. the floor, and align the splat to the grid with it. Straightens tilted scans.
sm.toolbar.overlays-tip: Show or hide helpers: grid, bounding box, cameras, dimensions and diagnostics.
sm.toolbar.sphere-brush-tip: A brush that paints on the surface and only selects splats near the spot it hits. What lies behind stays untouched.
sm.toolbar.titles-tip: Put text over the image, with timing, layout and style, e.g. for videos.
sm.toolbar.use-depth-tip: On: selects only the frontmost visible surface. Off: selects through all layers, hidden parts included.
sm.transform.scale-lock-tip: Locked: all three axes scale together. Unlocked: scale X, Y and Z separately (also with the per-axis handles of the scale tool).
sm.transform.xgrids-tip: Set the transform for XGrids scans (Z-up): position 0 0 0, rotation -90 0 0, scale 1
sm.transitions.add-in-tip: Build-up transition from the current frame (Shift+drag in the layer row works too)
sm.transitions.add-out-tip: Tear-down transition from the current frame (Shift+Alt+drag in the layer row)
sm.transitions.direction-tip: Axis for sweep and wave and for the swirl of fly-in. -Y with wave: rises from below
sm.transitions.drift-tip: Where the particles come from: outward from the origin, along the direction (e.g. +Y = from above) or random
sm.transitions.easing-tip: Pace of the transition: Linear even, In starts slow, Out ends slow, In-Out both.
sm.transitions.effect.dissolve-tip: Splats fly in as glowing particles and turn into splats. The front follows a noise pattern, an axis or the distance from the origin.
sm.transitions.effect.fly-tip: Splats start scattered and swirl into place.
sm.transitions.effect.grow-tip: Every splat grows from nothing, from the origin outward.
sm.transitions.effect.radial-tip: Builds the layer outward from the origin, behind a glowing front.
sm.transitions.effect.sweep-tip: Builds the layer along the direction, behind a glowing front.
sm.transitions.effect.wave-tip: Splats drop in along the direction with a small bounce. With -Y they rise from below.
sm.transitions.glow-tip: Strength of the glowing edge at the front
sm.transitions.noise-amount-tip: With axis/radial: how strongly the noise frays the front
sm.transitions.noise-freq-tip: Fineness of the noisy edge, relative to the layer size
sm.transitions.point-size-tip: Diameter of the glowing points in pixels
sm.transitions.points-first-tip: Splats first appear as points and turn into splats in the second half of their build.
sm.transitions.scatter-tip: Flight or fall distance relative to the layer size
sm.transitions.seed-tip: Random seed: a different number gives a different random pattern with the same settings.
sm.transitions.threshold-tip: What drives the dissolve front: pure noise, a direction (axis) or radial from the origin, each with a noise share
sm.transitions.timing-tip: Start frame and length of the transition, both in frames.
sm.transitions.title: Transitions
sm.video.alpha-tip: Keeps the background transparent (alpha channel) for compositing and social videos
sm.video.depth-tip: Adds a Z channel with the camera distance per pixel (scene units, empty = 1e10) to every EXR frame
sm.video.format-tip: MOV + PNG codec: lossless with alpha, for Premiere, After Effects, Resolve and Final Cut. WebM: alpha for the web. PNG / EXR sequence: one image per frame into a folder; EXR in linear light with an optional depth channel (Z) for compositing.
sm.video.shot-tip: Cut: renders the timeline cut as one video. Camera: only this camera's move. All cameras separately: one video per camera.
sm.viewport.tip: The view the viewport shows: free, through a camera or the cut. Click to switch.
